speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. To begin our evaluation, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation, or any changes in the color of your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The darkening of your urine combined with abdominal pain and fever is concerning; please confirm if you have noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice). REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel and Urinalysis. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_ULtrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 38.1°C (100.6°F), Blood Pressure 110/74 mm Hg, Heart Rate 99/min, Respiratory Rate Normal. General Exam: Appears tired, Mild scleral icterus observed. Abdominal Exam: Liver palpated 2–3 cm below right costal margin, tender on palpation. Lab Results: Hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, Leukocyte Count 11,600/mm3, Platelet Count 221,000/mm3, Urea Nitrogen 26 mg/dL, Glucose 122 mg/dL, Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL, Bilirubin Total 3.6 mg/dL, Bilirubin Direct 2.4 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 72 U/L, AST 488 U/L
